record.paper_title: On Open Problems of Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalues Problem
record.original_question: For a positive integer n, especially in the open range n >= 4 stated by the source, what are necessary and sufficient conditions for a multiset Lambda = {lambda_1, ..., lambda_n} of complex numbers to be exactly the spectrum, meaning the multiset of eigenvalues, of an n x n entrywise nonnegative matrix?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let n be a positive integer with n ≥ 4. Given a multiset Λ = {λ₁, λ₂, …, λₙ} of complex numbers (closed under complex conjugation), determine necessary and sufficient conditions on Λ for there to exist an n × n matrix A with real entries satisfying A_{ij} ≥ 0 for all i, j, whose multiset of eigenvalues (counted with algebraic multiplicities) equals Λ. Equivalently, characterize precisely which multisets of n complex numbers arise as the spectrum of some entrywise nonnegative n × n matrix.
artifact.status_search_result: The nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem (NIEP) is classically solved for n ≤ 4 but remains open for all n ≥ 5. The symmetric variant (SNIEP) is likewise solved only for n ≤ 4, with partial progress for n = 5 (e.g., the trace-zero case by Laffey–Meehan, 1999). No general necessary-and-sufficient characterization is known for n ≥ 5.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegative Inverse Eigenvalue Problem | IntechOpen
status_evidence.snippet: The NIEP is an open problem; a number of realizability criteria or sufficient conditions are known.
status_evidence.claim: The NIEP is open in general; only sufficient/necessary partial conditions are known.

status_evidence.title: The symmetric nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem for 5×5 matrices
status_evidence.snippet: SNIEP is solved for n ≤ 4 and remains open for n = 5.
status_evidence.claim: Even the symmetric variant is open at n = 5.

status_evidence.title: On the inverse eigenvalue problem for nonnegative matrices of order two to five
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses partial solutions up to order five.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are available for n = 5.
